answer_summary: A/AA counts in columns C18, C16, triplet C13, singlet C13 are respectively A = [2, 0, 0, 1] and AA = [0, 2, 0, 1].
assumptions: An sp cyclocarbon has two distinct cyclic pi manifolds, in-plane and out-of-plane.
Neutral even C_n supplies n pi electrons to each manifold.
Triplet C13 places one unpaired carbene electron in each manifold, giving populations 13 and 13.
For the elementary Huckel table, singlet C13 is interpreted as the conventional closed-shell singlet carbene with a paired/empty frontier-orbital distribution, giving populations 14 and 12.
A positive cyclic system with 4k+2 pi electrons is aromatic; one with positive 4k pi electrons is anti-aromatic; 4k+1 is neither under Huckel's rule.
source_gaps: The problem page gives only S = 0 for singlet C13 and does not print its orbital occupation. Spin zero alone does not logically exclude an open-shell singlet. The reported 1/1 entry follows the conventional closed-shell singlet-carbene interpretation intended by the elementary Huckel exercise; an open-shell 13/13 singlet would instead give 0/0. This boundary is explicitly documented rather than hidden.
